correctness.rationale: The differential is an area-one shear in an orthonormal polar frame, so its singular values give the exact dilatation. The hyperbolic displacement identity is exact for equal radii. Absolute continuity and the weighted derivative bound give \(|\phi(r)|\le S\log(1/r)\); \(2r\log(1/r)\le1-r^2\) then yields the \(\log K\) bound. Logarithmic twists have constant shear and approach the bound at the boundary, proving sharpness. The finite checker only tests algebraic identities and scalar envelopes and is not used as the proof.
